# Voice Pipes CLI Reference

**Status:** active
**Last verified:** 2026-09-06 (moved into the public tree; content unchanged)
**Owner:** Docs

`voice-pipes` is a local, modular voice pipeline that chains speech-to-text,
text processing, and text-to-speech stages into configurable pipelines.

Logs go to stderr in every command; stdout carries only the command's own
output (a transcript, `--format json` documents), so it can be piped into a
parser.

```
voice-pipes [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

## Synopsis

Output of `voice-pipes --help` and of every subcommand's `--help`.

```text
Voice Pipes -- local voice pipeline

Usage: voice-pipes [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  tts              Synthesize text to speech (text -> WAV)
  check            Run every component of a pipeline against known fixtures and report whether each did its job
  stt              Transcribe speech to text (WAV -> text)
  pipe             Round-trip pipeline: STT -> TTS (WAV -> text -> WAV)
  run              Run pipeline from a config file (WAV -> STT -> TTS -> WAV)
  serve            Start as a worker node (serves the pipeline + debug API)
  orchestrate      Start as the orchestrator (admin API + internal API)
  live             Live mic->STT->TTS->speaker loop (Ctrl+C to stop)
  listen           Listen: mic->STT only -- prints transcriptions (no LLM/TTS)
  interactive      Interactive real-time S2S voice loop client
  text             Run text through the text-processor chain (for testing LLM / echo / custom processors)
  inspect          List compiled-in providers, or print one provider's parameter schema
  validate-config  Validate a TOML config file: load it, run the same validation pass every other subcommand uses, and print a report. Exits non-zero on any validation error so it can be wired into CI
  healthz          Probe a health endpoint and exit 0 only on a success answer: the container images' `HEALTHCHECK`, which has no other HTTP client
  config-wizard    Launch interactive fleet configurator wizard to generate TOML configurations
  models           Download local model files, or list them, without the wizard
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>        Log format. Without it, `[pipeline] log_format` in the config decides, and compact lines when that is unset [possible values: compact, json]
      --captures-dir <CAPTURES_DIR>    Enable audit trail and write to this directory
      --audit-tap <SIDE>               Record audio around resampling stages for auditing. Values: before, after, both
      --audit-tap-dir <AUDIT_TAP_DIR>  Directory for audit tap WAV files (default: audit_tap/) [default: audit_tap]
      --config <PATH>                  Path to a TOML configuration file. Auto-discovers voice-pipes.toml in the current directory when not specified
  -h, --help                           Print help
  -V, --version                        Print version
```

### `check`

```text
Run every component of a pipeline against known fixtures and report whether each did its job.

Builds the components from the config file, so nothing needs to be running. Exits non-zero when a stage fails, so it can gate a deploy. Reports functional failures as well as measurement faults (`measurement.zero_with_work`, `measurement.invalid_numeric`).

Usage: voice-pipes check [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --fixture <NAME>
          Fixture to use, by name. Defaults to one with speech and one without, which test different failures

      --log-format <LOG_FORMAT>
          Log format. Without it, `[pipeline] log_format` in the config decides, and compact lines when that is unset
          
          [possible values: compact, json]

      --captures-dir <CAPTURES_DIR>
          Enable audit trail and write to this directory

      --audit-tap <SIDE>
          Record audio around resampling stages for auditing. Values: before, after, both

      --audit-tap-dir <AUDIT_TAP_DIR>
          Directory for audit tap WAV files (default: audit_tap/)
          
          [default: audit_tap]

      --config <PATH>
          Path to a TOML configuration file. Auto-discovers voice-pipes.toml in the current directory when not specified

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## Global Options

These flags apply to every subcommand.

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--config <PATH>` | auto-discover `voice-pipes.toml` | Path to a TOML configuration file |
| `--log-format <FMT>` | `compact` | Log output format: `compact` or `json` |
| `--captures-dir <DIR>` | *(disabled)* | Enable audit trail; write capture directories under this path |
| `--audit-tap <SIDE>` | *(disabled)* | Record audio around resampling stages (`before`, `after`, `both`) |
| `--audit-tap-dir <DIR>` | `audit_tap/` | Directory for audit-tap WAV files |

## Commands

### `tts` — Text to Speech

Synthesize text into a WAV file using the configured TTS provider.

```
voice-pipes tts --text <TEXT> [--output <FILE>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-t, --text` | yes | — | Text to synthesize |
| `-o, --output` | no | `output.wav` | Output WAV file path |

**Example**

```powershell
voice-pipes tts --text "Hello, world!" --output hello.wav
```

**Output** — writes `hello.wav` and logs synthesis metrics:

```
  INFO voice_pipes: loading TTS provider provider="piper"
  INFO voice_pipes: synthesizing text="Hello, world!"
  INFO voice_pipes: synthesis complete latency_ms=142 audio_duration_s="1.23" realtime_factor="8.66"
  INFO voice_pipes: WAV written output="hello.wav"
```

---

### `stt` — Speech to Text

Transcribe a WAV file to text using the configured STT provider.

```
voice-pipes stt --input <FILE>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-i, --input` | yes | — | Input WAV file path |

**Example**

```powershell
voice-pipes stt --input recording.wav
```

**Output** — prints the transcribed text to stdout:

```
Hello, world!
```

---

### `pipe` — Full Pipeline (STT → Text Processing → TTS)

Round-trip pipeline: transcribe a WAV, run text processors (e.g. LLM), then
re-synthesize back to audio.

```
voice-pipes pipe --input <FILE> [--output <FILE>] [--output-rate <HZ>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-i, --input` | yes | — | Input WAV file (audio to transcribe) |
| `-o, --output` | no | `output.wav` | Output WAV file (re-synthesized audio) |
| `--output-rate` | no | TTS native rate | Resample TTS output to this sample rate (e.g. `16000`, `48000`) |

**Example**

```powershell
voice-pipes pipe --input question.wav --output answer.wav --output-rate 48000
```

**Output** — writes `answer.wav` and logs each pipeline stage:

```
  INFO voice_pipes: loading providers stt="parakeet-tdt" tts="piper" text_processors=1
  INFO voice_pipes: reading WAV input="question.wav"
  INFO voice_pipes: transcribing samples=48000 sample_rate=16000 audio_duration_s="3.00"
  INFO voice_pipes: transcription complete text="What is the weather?" stt_latency_ms=210
  INFO voice_pipes: running text processor chain chain_len=1
  INFO voice_pipes: synthesizing text="The weather is sunny and 22 degrees."
  INFO voice_pipes: pipeline complete tts_latency_ms=95 output_duration_s="2.10" total_latency_ms=305
  INFO voice_pipes: WAV written output="answer.wav"
```

---

### `run` — Run Pipeline from Config

Alias for `pipe`. Reads input WAV, runs the full STT → text processing → TTS
pipeline, and writes output WAV.

```
voice-pipes run --input <FILE> [--output <FILE>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-i, --input` | yes | — | Input WAV file |
| `-o, --output` | no | `output.wav` | Output WAV file |

**Example**

```powershell
voice-pipes run --input prompt.wav --output response.wav
```

---

### `live` — Live Mic Loop

Real-time voice loop: captures mic audio, detects speech via VAD, transcribes
(STT), runs text processors (LLM), synthesizes a reply (TTS), and plays it
back through the speaker. Supports barge-in interruption.

Press **Ctrl+C** to stop.

```
voice-pipes live [--silence-ms <MS>] [--save-input <DIR>] [--save-output <DIR>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--silence-ms` | no | `1500` | Silence duration (ms) to mark end of utterance |
| `--save-input` | no | *(disabled)* | Save captured mic audio (one WAV per utterance) |
| `--save-output` | no | *(disabled)* | Save TTS output fragments (one WAV per chunk) |

**Example**

```powershell
voice-pipes live --silence-ms 1000 --save-input captures/mic --save-output captures/tts
```

**Output** — interactive session on the terminal:

```
🎤 Listening... speak and pause to trigger the pipeline. Ctrl+C to stop.

💬 (92%) What time is it?
  INFO voice_pipes: orchestrator: processing utterance utterance_id=1
🎤 Listening...

💬 (88%) Tell me a joke.
  INFO voice_pipes: orchestrator: processing utterance utterance_id=2
🎤 Listening...

👋 Stopped.
```

---

### `listen` — Listen Mode (STT Only)

Mic capture with STT transcription only — no LLM or TTS. Useful for testing
STT providers and VAD tuning.

Press **Ctrl+C** to stop.

```
voice-pipes listen [--silence-ms <MS>] [--save-input <DIR>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--silence-ms` | no | `1500` | Silence duration (ms) to mark end of utterance |
| `--save-input` | no | *(disabled)* | Save captured mic audio to this directory |

**Example**

```powershell
voice-pipes listen --silence-ms 2000 --save-input captures/
```

**Output** — prints each transcription as it arrives:

```
🎤 Listening (STT only)... speak and pause. Ctrl+C to stop.

[STT #001] (95%) Hello, can you hear me?
[STT #002] (91%) Testing, one two three.

👋 Stopped.
```

### `interactive` — Real-time Speech-to-Speech (S2S) Client

Terminal-native, real-time audio-in / audio-out client loop to test voice sessions directly with Gemini Live or OpenAI Realtime.

```
voice-pipes interactive --provider <PROVIDER> [--silence-ms <MS>] [--no-echo-gating]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--provider` | yes | — | S2S Provider: `gemini` (Gemini Live) or `openai` (OpenAI Realtime) |
| `--silence-ms` | no | `1500` | Silence duration (ms) to mark end of user utterance |
| `--no-echo-gating` | no | — | Disables client-side playback gating (mute mic while assistant responds). Recommended when wearing headphones to permit seamless spoken barge-ins |

**Example**

```powershell
voice-pipes interactive --provider gemini --silence-ms 1500 --no-echo-gating
```

**Key Features (Dual Keyboard + Voice Channel):**
- **Typewriter Text Reveal:** Display model's text segments as streaming, progressive captions.
- **Microphone Stream Muting:** Type `/mute` to dynamically mute and unmute your microphone.
- **Echo Gating Toggle:** Type `/gate` to dynamically enable or disable client-side microphone gating. Muting the mic while the model is speaking prevents acoustic loopback issues (such as echo/self-cancellation feedback or phantom translations when using open speakers). Turn off gating when testing with headphones so that you can barge in with your voice.
- **Chat via Text Prompting:** Type any normal sentence and hit **Enter** to write to the model.
- **Barge-In Interruption:** Hit **Enter** on an empty line while the model is speaking to immediately barge in and interrupt (silences speaker playbacks and stops model generation). Or, if echo-gating is disabled (headphones used), simply speak to trigger a server-side VAD barge-in.

---

### `serve` — Worker Node

Starts a worker node that exposes an HTTP debug API and an optional WebSocket
transport for client sessions. Optionally registers with an orchestrator for
fleet management.

```
voice-pipes serve [--worker-config <PATH>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--worker-config` | no | built-in defaults | Path to a worker config TOML file |

**Example**

```powershell
# Standalone worker with defaults
voice-pipes serve

# Worker that registers with an orchestrator
voice-pipes serve --worker-config worker.toml
```

**Output** — the worker binds and logs readiness:

```
  INFO voice_pipes: worker debug API listening bind="127.0.0.1:9090" worker_id="a3f1..."
  INFO voice_pipes: transport listener started (WebSocket) bind="0.0.0.0:8800" max_sessions=4
  INFO voice_pipes: worker node ready & registered with orchestrator
```

The debug API is available at `http://<debug_bind>:<debug_port>/` with
endpoints for health, config introspection, and session status.

**Port fallback** — if a configured port is already in use (common when running
multiple workers locally), the worker automatically tries the next port, up to
16 consecutive ports. A warning is logged when a fallback port is used:

```
  WARN voice_pipes: transport (WebSocket): port 8800 already in use, trying next…
  WARN voice_pipes: transport (WebSocket): configured port 8800 was unavailable, bound to 8801 instead
```

If all 16 ports are occupied, startup fails with a clear error:

```
  transport (WebSocket): ports 8800–8815 are all in use — free a port or choose a different range
```

The actual bound port is sent in the registration payload, so the orchestrator
always routes to the correct address regardless of fallback.

---

### `orchestrate` — Orchestrator Node

Starts the orchestrator that manages a fleet of worker nodes. Exposes an admin
API (worker list, session history, benchmarks) and an internal API (worker
registration, heartbeats).

```
voice-pipes orchestrate [--orchestrator-config <PATH>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--orchestrator-config` | no | built-in defaults | Path to an orchestrator config TOML file |

**Example**

```powershell
voice-pipes orchestrate --orchestrator-config orchestrator.toml
```

**Output** — the orchestrator binds and begins accepting worker registrations:

```
  INFO voice_pipes: orchestrator API listening bind="0.0.0.0:8080"
```

The same port-fallback logic applies: if port 8080 is taken, successive ports
are tried. A warning reminds you to update worker configs to point at the new
port:

```
  WARN voice_pipes: orchestrator bound to a different port — workers must target port 8081
```

---

### `text` — Text Processor Chain

Runs input text through the configured text-processor chain (LLM, echo,
custom APIs) without any audio processing. Useful for testing LLM prompts
and processor pipelines.

```
voice-pipes text [--input <TEXT>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-i, --input` | no | reads from stdin | Input text to process |

**Example**

```powershell
# Inline text
voice-pipes text --input "Summarize quantum computing."

# Pipe from stdin
echo "Translate to French: Good morning" | voice-pipes text
```

**Output** — prints the processed text to stdout:

```
  INFO voice_pipes: processing text text="Summarize quantum computing." chain_len=1

>> Quantum computing uses qubits to perform calculations exponentially faster than classical computers for certain problems.
```

---

### `check` — Check Every Component

Builds each component of the configured pipeline — VAD, recogniser, text
processors, synthesiser — and runs it alone against a shipped recording with
known words, reporting per stage whether it did its job: how much speech the
VAD dropped before the onset, the transcript against the expected words, the
model's reply and time to first token, the synthesiser's real-time factor.
Nothing needs to be running. These are the same checks as the admin
console's Component check and the worker's `/debug/probe/*` endpoints.

```
voice-pipes --config <PATH> check [--fixture <NAME>]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--fixture` | no | one recording with speech and one without | Fixture to use, by name (see `voice-pipes/fixtures/manifest.json`) |

Exits non-zero when any stage fails, so it can gate a deploy.

---

### `models` — Fetch Local Model Files

Downloads model files to their default locations, without the wizard's
questions. The names are the wizard's model registry
(`voice-pipes/config/wizard_models.json`, plus what linked plugins declare).
Paths are relative to the working directory; run from the repository root, the
command moves into `voice-pipes/`, where the example configs expect them.

```
voice-pipes models fetch [NAME...]
voice-pipes models list
```

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `models fetch` | With no names, the set `examples/minimal.toml` needs: `parakeet`, `silero`, `piper`, `smollm2-360m`. Files already on disk are skipped. |
| `models fetch smollm2-1.7b moonshine` | The named entries only. An unknown name is refused with the list of known ones. |
| `models list` | Every entry, its default path, and whether its files are present. |

Gated models (the Gemma entries) need `HF_TOKEN`. Exits non-zero when a
download fails.

---

## Configuration

All commands read from a TOML config file. By default, `voice-pipes.toml` in
the current directory is auto-discovered. Override with `--config <PATH>`.

The smallest complete example is
[`voice-pipes/examples/minimal.toml`](../../voice-pipes/examples/minimal.toml):
VAD, Parakeet, an in-process SmolLM2 and Piper, all fetched by
`voice-pipes models fetch`.

See `02-CONFIGURATION.md` for the full config reference.

---

## Exit Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Runtime error (config validation failure, provider error, I/O error), or a failed stage in `check` |
